title: introduce-graph-checkpointing-and-relaxed-shape-guards-to-mitigate-cudagraph-warmup-regressions
author: Aisha Chopra
description: Motivation: Recent CUDA graph capture/replay changes improved steady-state throughput but introduced warmup regressions and brittle shape-guard failures on long-context workloads. This PR implements a defensive checkpointing layer around cudagraph captures and a relaxed shape-guard reconciliation strategy at replay time to reduce spurious fallbacks and decrease warmup iterations. The change bundle includes three coordinated pieces: 1) lightweight graph checkpointing: during capture we snapshot minimal allocator + KV cache alignment state and allow replay to restore to that checkpoint when a replay mismatch occurs, reducing failed replays that trigger full fallback; 2) relaxed shape guards: instead of immediately invalidating a cudagraph on minor shape mismatches (e.g., trailing padding, small attention-mask permutations), the runtime now attempts an incremental patch path up to N times before falling back; 3) KV cache capture alignment: avoid extra KV reallocations during capture by aligning chunked cache buffers to the graph's expected KV layout, which reduces memory churn and a class of racey mismatches seen under continuous batching. This PR also adds metrics (cudagraph.checkpoint.restore_count, cudagraph.guard_patch_attempts, cudagraph.forced_fallbacks) and a canary rollout/config flag (cudagraph.enable_checkpointing) to control behavior per-deployment. Benchmark summary (internal perf runner): - GPT-like 8k seq, warmup iterations reduced from ~18->6 on average for 1-2 stream workloads - Steady-state throughput unchanged (+1% variance) - Regression test: reduces incidence of forced fallbacks from 4.8%->0.9% across synthetic masking permutations Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration test for replay mismatches - [x] Metrics and traces added - [x] Canary flag and migration docs - [x] Perf regression validated on perf-canary infra Known limitations/notes: - In some pathological multi-tenant burst patterns, checkpoint restore still falls back to non-cudagraph route after the configurable retry budget; we track metrics to identify customers to opt into extended budgets. - This does not change capture semantics for models with dynamic weights; those still bypass cudagraph. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable as opt-in on staging, run perf-canary across 48h window, flip default after 1 week if no increase in cudagraph.forced_fallbacks or host-level OOMs. Related work: follows up on ENG-7067 (cudagraph warmup investigation) and builds on kernel scheduling patches in PRs that changed capture ordering.
commits: 3 commits: a) runtime: add checkpointing layer and checkpoint store with TTL and atomic restore (Aisha Chopra) b) runtime: implement relaxed shape-guard reconciliation + retry budget + metrics (Marcus Li) c) tests/docs: integration tests for replay mismatches and canary config (Hannah Kim)

review_thread: Marcus Li (review): overall approach looks solid; please add more comments around atomicity guarantees in checkpoint_store and a small diagram in docs showing lifecycle.
Aisha Chopra (reply): added comments and diagram; reworked checkpoint ttl logic to use eviction hook instead of polling.

Hannah Kim (review): observed a flaky integration test on CI that failed under py3.10 container; suspect timing of deferred destructor in allocator mock. Requested a fix and an additional CI job variant.
Aisha Chopra (reply): fixed destructor ordering and added a CI matrix job (ubuntu-py3.10) to catch regression. Reran perf tests and included results in PR description.
Diego Rivera (approval): Verified metrics on staging canary, smoke-tested with a 2-node dedicated pool. Approving for merge after green CI and doc updates.
release_notes: Add cudagraph checkpointing to reduce warmup regressions and relaxed shape guard reconciliation to lower spurious fallbacks. Opt-in via cudagraph.enable_checkpointing. Metrics added for observability.
